name: Caiaphas
overview: Caiaphas was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as the High Priest during the time of the Messiah's last Passover. His role as High Priest situates him at a critical moment in biblical history, overseeing religious duties in Jerusalem. No additional personal notes are recorded about him in the provided facts.
namesAndTitles: The name Caiaphas appears as a proper name without any given meaning or divine origin indicated in the Scriptures. It is simply the name by which he is known, as referenced in Matthew 26:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Caiaphas as a descendant of Aaron, the first High Priest, which aligns with his Levitical heritage and priestly office. Beyond this lineage, no further family relationships are detailed in the available information.
scriptureSignificance: Caiaphas holds significance as the High Priest at the pivotal moment of the Messiah's final Passover, a time central to the unfolding of God's redemptive plan. His priestly leadership during this period places him in direct contact with the events leading to Christ's passion. This connection underscores his role in the religious and judicial processes that affected Jesus' earthly ministry.
